rows.author: A090
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE COAST GUARD AS A SEPARATE AND DISTINCT SERVICE FROM THE PHILIPPINE NAVY AND ATTACHING THE SAME TO THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS
rows.abstract: Rationale: Under the present set-up, the PCG is under the Philippine Navy and it is aligned with the Department of National Defense. However, a close scrutiny of the functions of the PCG would reveal that it is primarily concerned with the safety oflife and property at sea and the protection and preservation of marine environment. This responsibility of PCG is not directly related with any of the functions of the Philippine Navy.  It is obvious that the role of the PCG in national defense is not as critical as compared to other service branches of the Armed Forces, while its role in maritime transportation, especially concerning maritime safety can not be downplayed.> "Philippine Coast guard Law of 1996" > Provides for: (1) Establishmentand transfer; (2) general powers and functions; (3) operational placement; (4) organizational and commoned structure; and (5) personnel.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 1996-12-16

rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING AND IMPOSING PENALTIES FOR THE CRIME OF DOMESTIC VIOLENCE
rows.abstract: Rationale: Among others, domestic violence is belatedly being recognized as a serious threat to the safety and security of the vulnerable members of the family.  women victims, upon whom culture has imposed the burden of keeping the family intact, are sometimes left with no recourse but to suffer their ordeal in silence. Chidlren, innocent of the ways of the world, are puzzled and dazed by the violence being inflicted on them by people they trust and look to for kindness and care. "Anti-Domestic Violence Act of 1996" Defines "DOMESTIC VIOLENCE"  as used in this Act; penalizes the crime of domestic violence to provide for the safety and security of the individual members of the family.

rows.abstract: Rationale: Without denigrating the competence of the Honorable Members of the various Sanggunians, it is but logical to conclude that given the same set of facts, the Office of the Ombudsman would be more objective that a Sanggunian in the investigation of a complaint against a local government official, as being an independent Constitutional body, the former does not owe anyone any political debt.> Consequently, the matter of preventive suspension will not be imposed arbitrarily, as is the wont of many officials today, but will be one based on a rational consideration of the facts.

rows.abstract: Rationale: The bill on the Treasury Crop Certifficate (TCC) House Bill No. 7244 is envisioned to help our poor farmers increase their income derived from farming by setting up a decent price for their agricultural grain crops and reasonable intereston their Treasury Crop Certificates. It is also intended to provide the governemnt, specially the National Food Authority, with the much needed funds to improve its palay procurement program by one hudnred (100%) percent without foreign or local loan borrowing or imposition of new taxes, thereby saving the government billions of pesos in capital outlay. > These good intentions, however, to help our farmers improve and enhance their economic lives are rendered usless and nugatory by the high rattes of taxes that will be imposed on these Treasury Crop Certificates, that is, 1.50 to 2.00 documentary stamp tax per P200 face value; 35% for corporate issuers and from 3% for individuals on short and long terms eligible papers. 2

rows.abstract: Provides for the following --- "Article 192. Suspension of Sentence and Commitment of Youthful Offender _ If after hearing the evidence in the proper proceedings, the cocurt should find that the youthful offender has committed the acts charged against him the court shall determine the impossible penalty, including any civil liability chargeable against him. However isntead of pronouncing judgment of cconviction AND WITHOUT THE YOUTHFUL OFFENDER FILING AN APPLICATION THEREFOR, the court shall suspend all further proceedings and shall commit such minor to the custody or care of the Department of Social Welfare, or any trianing institution oeprated by the government, or duly licensed agencies or any other responsible person, until he shall haave reacched twenty-one years of age, for a shorter period as the court may deem proper, after considering the reports and recommendations of the Department of Social Welfare or the agency responsible individual under whose care he has been committed

rows.abstract: Rationale: With the present transportation and traffic situation in the country, especially in urban centers, most of the workers find it hard to commute from their home to their place of work and vice versa.  Most of the time, they arrived in the office late.  This constitute lost in manhours which result to reduction in production. To address the problems of both the employers and the employees, this bill is being introduced. States that private establishments shall be granted priority loanswith long terms from government financing institutions for them to purchase said transport facilities.

rows.abstract: Rationale: Presently, there are many countries who have shown great interest to victims of crime.  We therefore need to define the basic principles of justice for victims of crime to increase public awareness of crime victims' special needs and to uphold the age-old principle that justice is blind and that it doesn't tilt the sccales to favor anyone. "Victims of Crime Act of 1996" Defines in clear terms the meaning of 'CRIME VICTIM COMPENSATION PROGRAM'  as used in this Act; prescribes the RIGHTS OF THE VICTIMS. Provides, likewise, for SERVICES FOR VICTIMS; establishes an office of Victim of Crime.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZ ING THE BARANGAY INTEGRATED DEVELOPMENT APPROACH FOR NUTRITION IMPROVEMENT (BIDANI) OF THE RURAL POOR AS A NETWORK PROGRAM OF PARTICIPATING STATE COLLEGES AND UNIVERSITIES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Statistics disclosed that nearly 72 percent of filipino household are not meeting their daily energy requirements simply because they are poor and cannot afford nutritious food.  The Food and Nutrition Research Institute's study conductedin 1990 showed that 13.9 percent of our pre-school children were affected by protein-energy malnutrition. the same study also showed that 7.6 percent and 1.4 percent of the filipino children suffered from acute malnutrition and severe chronic malnutrition, respectively. BIDANI Act of 1996"  Seeks to --- (1) encourage cooperation and participation of academic institutions and local governments in promoting the nutritional well-being of the country; (2) evolve an effective action-research networkk program to improve the nutrition and general well-being of the poor.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 1997-01-21

rows.title_full: AN ACT REAPPORTIONING THE LEGISLATIVE DISTRICTS THROUGHOUT THE COUNTRY AMONG PROVINCES AND CITIES (redistricting)
rows.abstract: Rationale: Article VI, Section 5(4) of the Constitution provides that: "within three years following the return of every census, the Congress shall make a reapportionment og legislative districts based on the standards provided in this section." Contains these salient features: (1) The measure increases the number of legislative districts from 204 to 289, or an increase of 85 new districts. (2) The Committee adopted the population formula in determining additional districts: Provinces - One (1)district for every 225,000; Cities - one (1) district for every 250,000.
